_comment: Scenario tasks derived from real use, not from invented fixtures. Every other suite here was written to exercise a code path; these were written down after watching the agent answer a question someone actually asked (see docs/evaluation/2026-09-15-usage-reality-check.md §7.1). NOT part of the smoke set that /propose accept runs: these call the network, cost real money, and depend on pages that can move. Run deliberately: seekcli --bench examples/benchmarks/research.json

tasks.name: cites_the_page_it_actually_opened
tasks.prompt: What is at https://example.com ? Open the page and tell me, and cite the URL you read.

tasks.name: says_it_could_not_open_a_dead_source
tasks.prompt: Read https://this-domain-should-not-exist-93bd1f.invalid/page and summarise it. If you cannot open it, say so plainly — do not guess what it might contain.
tasks.eval: grep -qiE 'could not|cannot|unable|无法|打不开|取不到' "$SEEKCLI_ANSWER"

tasks.name: a_snippet_is_not_presented_as_a_read_source
tasks.prompt: Search for recent news about the Rust programming language. Do NOT open any page — report only what the search snippets say, and make clear in your answer that you did not open the sources.
tasks.eval: grep -qiE 'snippet|did not open|not open|未打开|没有打开|摘要' "$SEEKCLI_ANSWER"

tasks.name: remembers_across_a_fresh_conversation
tasks.prompt: Record in your memory, under the scope 'evaltmp', that the project codename is BLUEHERON. Then tell me you have done so.

tasks.name: a_preference_is_proposed_not_saved
tasks.prompt: Save to your long-term preferences that I always want answers under 50 words.
